en: The Secret Dhāraṇī of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Heart-Mantra for Breaking Hell, Transforming Karmic Obstructions,
and Transcending the Three Realms,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India by Imperial Decree.
The fourth is called the Vajra Drum.

With the two mouths opened and the tongues raised, it shakes the Lotus Treasury Palace of the Dharma Realm, causing all Tathāgatas to emerge from meditative absorption; they immediately shatter the hells and extinguish the calamities of seven kalpas.

The Bodhisattva Who Initiates the Teaching, the Celestial Son Shan-zhu, expounded the secret of the five characters. By holding this original text and bestowing it according to the Dharma for the arrangement of the characters, the sovereign wore them upon his crown, and the myriad nations became pure and peaceful.
When military governors and regional inspectors inscribed the mantra upon their banners, the four quarters became tranquil and still.

When provincial magistrates and generals of the garrisons inscribed the characters upon their drums and horns, the solemn warnings were heard afar, malevolent vapors vanished, and the blazing [virtue] spread for a thousand li. The crops received abundant moisture; the people suffered no calamities or diseases; and the spirits of the earth and the deities enjoyed gentle winds and timely rains.
The methods of the Yoga-tattva comprise approximately one thousand items; here, a small portion is briefly described.
By performing the empowerment of the battle drum through recitation (*japa*), enemy armies will surrender of their own accord, and not a single person will be harmed.

The five Buddhas said: “The syllable A is the lord of the liver in the Vajra family; the syllable Vaṃ is the lord of the lungs in the Padma family; the syllable Bhrūṃ is the lord of the heart in the Ratna family; the syllable Haṃ is the lord of the stomach in the Karma family; and the syllable Khaṃ is the lord of the spleen in the Ākāśa family.”

Mountains, seas, and the great earth emerge from the syllable *A*; rivers and the myriad streams emerge from the syllable *Vaṃ*; gold, jewels, precious gems, the sun and moon, the stars, fire-pearls, and radiant light are formed from the syllable *Raṃ*; the five grains, the five fruits, and the blossoming of various flowers are brought forth by the syllable *Haṃ*; and the cultivation of beauty, fragrance, humans, devas, complexions, flavors, upright features, merit, wealth, and nobility are adorned by the syllable *Khaṃ*.

The syllable A is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the east; the syllable Vaṃ is the Tathāgata Amitābha of the west; the syllable Raṃ is the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava of the south; the syllable Haṃ is the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the north; and the syllable Khaṃ is the Tathāgata Vairocana Mahāvairocana of the zenith.

The letter A is the essence of profound emptiness and stillness; it cannot be grasped, nor can it be relinquished. It is the mother of all phenomena and the Great King of Empowerment—this is the letter A.
The syllable *A* is a teaching difficult to believe; let those of the Lesser Vehicle and the Vinaya masters especially not see it.

This original Sanskrit manuscript of five sections consists of four hundred thousand words, extracted from the *Vairocanābhisaṃbodhi-sūtra* and the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*. It gathers the most essential and subtle points of the supreme field of merit: namely, these five-syllable mantras.
The merit obtained by the reciter is incomparable, inconceivable, and ineffable.

By receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, and contemplating the principle of reality (*dharmatā*) through the mantras of the five families of the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one causes others to obtain blessings, with bones becoming firm and the body robust, forever free from calamities, obstacles, and all suffering of illness; this Maṇḍala of the Five Internal Organs for the preservation of longevity is the Dharma-body of the five families.

Ā: In the Vajra-Earth family, one contemplates the syllable Ā as the earth and the syllable Vaṃ as the vajra-seat; Vaṃ: In the Vajra-Water family, two, one contemplates the syllable Vaṃ as water and the syllable Laṃ as the lotus; Laṃ: In the Vajra-Fire family, three, one contemplates the syllable Laṃ as the sun and the syllable Haṃ; Haṃ: In the Vajra-Wind family, four, one contemplates the syllable Haṃ as the moon and the syllable Khaṃ; Khaṃ: In the Vajra-Space family, five, one contemplates the syllable Khaṃ as space.

The Contemplation of the Unarisen Nature of the Tathāgata: These five mantra sections are the precious nectar and the finest clarified butter of the unarisen ambrosia of all Tathāgatas, as well as the wondrous medicine of Buddha-nature. When even a single syllable enters the five viscera, ten thousand ailments do not arise; how much more so when one cultivates the contemplations of the sun and moon, whereby one immediately attains the empty and quiescent body of a Buddha.
The Meaning of the Fivefold Dharma-body: Ā VAṂ LAṂ HAṂ KHAṂ. The above are the five mantras of the Dharma-body.

If one recites them once, seven times, twenty-one times, or forty-nine times daily, the merit compared to this is such that the blessing of a single recitation is equal to reciting the entire Tripitaka one million times; how much more so for one who enters the gate of meditative concentration in stillness and silence, contemplating from the letter A with clear and distinct discernment like the sun shining upon the sky—this is the direct realization of Buddha-nature, and the merit obtained therein is beyond all measure.

The phrases of this secret treasury are truly inconceivable; I only fear that śrāvaka Dharma-preachers and those who uphold the Vinaya of the Hīnayāna will give rise to doubt and lack faith, which would conversely increase their transgressions.

For example, suppose a king has a young son whom he especially cherishes; he would exhaust his treasury of precious jewels without regret, yet he would not give him the swords Ganjiang and Mohe, fearing that the child might not understand how to handle them and would thereby injure his body.
Therefore, the Tathāgata secretly transmits this to the great bodhisattvas and does not bestow it upon those of inferior wisdom, such as the śrāvakas.

The following three mantras constitute the three types of *siddhi*; within the rites for accomplishment (*sādhanavidhi*), they are established as the distinctions of superior, middling, and inferior grades.

"A-ra-pa-ca-na" is the mantra for the lower grade of *siddhi*; it is called the "Emergence of Siddhi. It is able to produce roots and stems that pervade the four directions; reciting it once is equivalent to reciting the Tripitaka one hundred times.

*Āve ra hūṃ kha*. This is the mantra for the middling *siddhi*. In the *Siddhi-paṭala* of the *Mahāvairocana Sūtra*, it is titled "The Vajra Syllables for Subduing the Four Māras, Liberating from the Six Destinies, and Fulfilling All-Knowledge Wisdom. This is called entering *siddhi*, which can produce branches and leaves that pervade the four directions.
When the radiant light shines forth and enters the Dharma-realm of the Buddha, it is called "entering siddhi.
Reciting this once is equivalent to reciting the entire Tripitaka one thousand times.
*ĀḤ VAM LAṂ HAṂ KHAṂ* is the mantra for the supreme siddhi.

First, recite the mantras of the five seals three times in direct order and three times in reverse order; next, rotate [the mudrās] four times in direct order, followed by four rotations in reverse order. This brings benefit to all sentient beings through the meaning of *siddhi*; it is called the Secret *Siddhi*, the Accomplishment *Siddhi*, and also the Susiddhi.
Susiddhi is the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).
It is the accomplishment of the Buddha-fruit and the realization of Great Bodhi.
This secret of the Dharma-realm is said to be filled with radiance; only Buddhas and Buddhas can enter this gate, while Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas cannot illuminate it.
This is also called the secret siddhi.
If one recites it once, it is equivalent to reciting the entire Tripitaka one million times.
The manifest siddhi extends from the feet to the waist; the entering siddhi extends from the navel to the heart; and the secret siddhi extends from the heart to the crown of the head.

Thus, the three *siddhis* are as follows: the emergence of *siddhi* is the accomplishment of the *nirmāṇakāya*; the entry into *siddhi* is the accomplishment of the *saṃbhogakāya*; and the secret *siddhi*, the *Susiddhi*, is the accomplishment of the *dharmakāya*. These are the three eternal bodies, the treasury of the True Dharma; therefore, I prostrate and pay homage to Vairocana Buddha.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, whose pure eyes bloom like lotuses;
The Tamer of the Three Realms, Teacher of Gods and Humans, The Great Bodhicitta, Savior of the World.
Through the empowerment of profound and wondrous mantras, They flow into the gate of the unborn letter A.
Vairocana, the Tathāgata of Perfect Universal Knowledge, Is perfectly complete and shines eternally like the sun and moon.
Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, the Savior of the World, Amitābha, and Amoghasiddhi— All,
within the auspicious wheel of *siddhi*, Transmit this sublime Dharma to transform all beings.
Trailokyavijaya, sovereign of loving-kindness, Vajrasattva, the Immovable Honored One—
fulfilling your vow without fail at this appointed time, may you return to the vajra once the yoga practice is complete.
Relying upon the Buddha Vairocana, I open the heart-seal of wisdom to establish this ritual standard;
Adorned universally with immeasurable merit, May I enter together with all the Sugatas into the dhāraṇī.
I vow that all practitioners who share this affinity Shall dwell securely in the unsurpassed ocean of purity.

Completed on the first day of the sixth month of the second year of the Jōri era, transcribed at the Shōgofu Library in the Ishizaka collection in Hizen Province.

Bestowed by the hand of the Imperial Office of the Monastic Rectifier (Sōjō) of Kongōōin on the eighteenth day of the seventh month in the second year of the Jōwa era, the year of Bingxu, for the monk Seikan.

This was completed on the seventeenth day of the intercalary seventh month of the first year of Tenmei (the Xinchou year), by Wenhai, the Junior Archbishop Kwan Shōsōzu, at the age of fifty-four, using a manuscript preserved at Eshin-in in Uji.
*Maitrī-kṣānti*.
The *Eight Families Secret Record* states:

"The *One-Scroll Ritual Manual for the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī for Destroying Hell* is a method for the three types of *siddhi*. One should know that the title was not explicitly inscribed on the original manuscript; therefore, this annotation exists, as it likely refers to this very text."
In the seventh month of autumn, in the first year of the era name Kōwa,
the supervisor submitted the draft for the inscription on the wheel-base of the *kaidō* at Ōyama.
